correctness.rationale: For every 0<p<1 except p=1/2, conditional uniformity on dyadic cells gives an exact countable Markov chain. The left-branch gambler’s-ruin solution yields theta=(1-delta)/(1+3delta), then fresh geometric-depth crossings yield independent excursions and a geometric return count. The right-sojourn pgf follows from g=z(P+Q g^2) and b=Pz/(1-Qzg), yielding the algebraic occupation pgf and its exact derivative. Explicit near-critical square-root expansion gives the Laplace law. Renewal is almost surely finite and the strong law gives the endpoint logarithmic exponent; reflection covers the other bias direction. Tests in verify.py completed 91 exact/symbolic/finite-sample checks. Stochastic experiments are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The identified primary results describe equal-probability, recurrent Hata map arcsine laws and equal-probability geometrically deformed maps. They do not imply the asserted offcritical finite return count, complete occupation generating function, exact means, two crossover laws, or endpoint exponent. Semantic searches and related published dynamical findings did not identify a stronger or equivalent statement. Unavailable 2019 thesis and unindexed work remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The Hata random interval map is a canonical critical intermittency example. The natural half-return count and total unfavored-half occupation have finite offcritical laws absent at the recurrent critical parameter. The exact transform distinguishes inverse-bias and inverse-square-bias scales with two different universal limits and gives the almost-sure endpoint attraction exponent. This answers motivated quantitative transient questions for a structurally meaningful parameter perturbation, rather than an arbitrary enumeration or routine re-labeling.
